title: Learning distinguishes meditation styles in experienced monks’ brain connectivity
summary: A linear support-vector machine distinguished focused-attention from open-monitoring fMRI connectivity patterns in twelve experienced monks, with reported internal accuracy of 65.6%; classification was not significant in ten novice meditators. Model inspection implicated salience and default-mode connections. This small observational comparison does not establish that meditation training caused the differences. Caption and Methods differ on whether validation splits separated participants or repeated samples, so unseen-person generalization is not established.
ai_technology: Linear support-vector machine; training-fold ANOVA feature selection
organization: University of Chieti-Pescara; Sapienza University of Rome

source_review.scope: Primary relevant participant/task, connectivity and SVM Methods, validation/results and discussion; exact article-meta DOI/title/PMCID/date and current PubMed notice relationships. Supplementary ROI table not inspected.

evidence.tested: Internal fMRI-connectivity classification of two meditation styles in twelve experienced and ten novice male meditators, with training-fold feature selection and label permutations. Reported style accuracy was 65.6% in experts and 54.4% in novices, the latter not significant.
evidence.unknown: Independent subject-level validation and causal training effects remain unestablished. Fig.1 describes participant-level splitting while the Methods describe sample-level splitting; repeated blocks and model-weight interpretations limit generalization. The small groups differ in experience, age and recruitment.
evidence.ai_role: The linear SVM learns combinations of between-region functional connectivity that distinguish the two recorded meditation conditions; feature-selection frequency and learned weights identify connections contributing to that discrimination.
